title: 1956 AHSME Problem 17
statement: The fraction \(\dfrac{5x-11}{2x^2+x-6}\) was obtained by adding the two fractions \(\dfrac A{x+2}\) and \(\dfrac B{2x-3}.\) The values of \(A\) and \(B\) must be, respectively:

solutions.text:
Combining the proposed partial fractions gives \[ \frac{A(2x-3)+B(x+2)}{(x+2)(2x-3)}. \] Matching its numerator with \(5x-11\) yields \[ \begin{aligned} 2A+B&=5,\\ -3A+2B&=-11. \end{aligned} \] Solving gives \(A=3\) and \(B=-1.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: After combining the two fractions, match coefficients in \(A(2x-3)+B(x+2)=5x-11\)
